name: Skinner Out of Touch
aka: Am I So Out of Touch
No, It's the Children Who Are Wrong
look: Two stacked frames from The Simpsons. Principal Skinner, in a dark suit and red tie, stands before a city skyline with a dark curtain and cobwebs at the edges. Top: he strokes his chin in thought. Bottom: he stares ahead, wide-eyed and self-assured.
use: Someone briefly wonders if they are the problem, then decides everyone else is wrong. The top caption voices the doubt, like "Am I out of touch?", and the bottom blames others: "No, it's the ___ who are wrong."
examples: Is my phone always dead because I never charge it?
No, it's the battery that is wrong
Am I bad at this game?
No, it's my teammates who are wrong
describe: simpsons principal thinking then deciding everyone else is wrong
cartoon principal with hand on chin then wide eyed stare
man in suit wonders if he is the problem then blames others
two panel simpsons denial meme about the kids being wrong
simpsons character stroking his chin then looking confident
origin: Principal Skinner's line "Am I so out of touch? No, it's the children who are wrong" from The Simpsons.
